results.change: Found the root cause beyond the reviewer's diagnosis: facing the camera, Run_Right is a strafe that travels toward screen-left (its stance foot moves +X), so the legs ran toward the wave while the root moved right, a true moonwalk. Switched to the mirror clip Run_Left at speed 0.8. To keep the original composition (root path -0.05 -> 0.2, start upright at screen x~744, wave lip at 'carved'), the root runs at constant speed with a 0.15 s ramp-in matching the clip fade and a 0.06 s stop at the hit. The tiny planet turns under him (about Z, P2 = W2 - 1.75*0.8/3 rad/s) for the rest of the stride, which is the engine's tiny-planet technique, so the stance foot stays fixed to the ground. The planet keeps its final roll afterwards, including in the close-up. A pure speed-matched root without the rolling planet was tried first and rejected: it put him tilted 22 deg at the frame's left edge.

result.shared_changes_needed: None. All fixes are in ch1.js only; ch1_fx.js and ch1_ee.js are unchanged. Two shared quirks were worked around locally, with no shared change required: (1) shots.js camAt applies only the destination key's ease, so an ease on keys[0] is silently ignored (also at ch1 keys for the paleo flash, s008 and the 'last' spin, which read smoothly and were left alone). (2) geo.js findFeature also matches SOVEREIGNT and returns the first hit, so a lookup by full country name can return a territory. A later shared cleanup could match ADMIN/NAME/ISO before SOVEREIGNT.
